findings.title: Signed transaction not verified against preview (backend trusted for taker/creator funds)
findings.severity_scope: malicious/compromised backend or MITM; contracts remain safe
findings.intended_invariant: I9 preview truthfulness: the signed tx does what the preview claims
findings.attack: Frontend signs backend-provided CBOR verbatim and renders a backend-provided summary; only the fee is decoded from the real tx. A hostile backend returns a benign summary with a CBOR that routes the taker's/creator's own wallet UTxOs to attacker outputs or a hostile change address. On-chain value conservation permits it because the signer authors the tx; validators only pin the seller's payment.
findings.concrete_example: Take order shows 'pay 50 tADA, receive TOKEN'; CBOR sets change address to attacker so the user's whole wallet drains. Only the wallet dialog reveals it.
findings.actual_result: Validators accept the tx; taker robbed; no client-side check besides wallet UI (documented as a known gap).
findings.impact: Theft of taker/creator funds under backend compromise. Sellers unaffected.
findings.proof_of_concept: Direct code path: confirmAndSign -> signAndSubmit(wallet, state.tx.unsignedTxCborHex) with no re-derivation; STANDARD_WARNINGS and TransactionPreview comment acknowledge it.
findings.regression_test: Frontend test that decodes returned CBOR and asserts all non-fee/non-change outputs, change address, and mint match the summary; reject on mismatch (not yet present).
findings.recommended_fix: Client-side decode the unsigned CBOR before signing and assert change==wallet change, every external output matches a summary line (addr+value+datum incl PaymentTag), and mint==summary beacon set; reject otherwise. Add reproducible-build script-hash attestation.

findings.title: Mint policy does not bound ask asset identifier length -> unfillable order-book spam
findings.intended_invariant: I7/I10 only real, fillable, correctly-formed orders enter the book
findings.attack: The ask asset is never held in the order UTxO, so mint_beacons_ok never checks datum.ask.policy_id (28B) or datum.ask.asset_name (<=32B) length. A raw creation tx (bypassing backend, which caps at 32B) creates an order asking for a non-existent asset (e.g. 40-byte name). It mints and indexes but can never be taken.
findings.concrete_example: ask={policy_id:<28B>, asset_name:0xaabb...(40 bytes)}, ask_amount=1, offer 100 TOKA, deposit 3.5 ADA -> mints, shows on pair, never fillable.
findings.impact: Order-book pollution/griefing; degraded UX. Not theft (offer side is bounded by real assets). Deposit-limited.
findings.regression_test: Same test; a fix should flip it to fail.
findings.recommended_fix: In mint_beacons_ok require (is_ada(ask) || bytearray.length(ask.policy_id)==28) and bytearray.length(ask.asset_name)<=32 (and same for offer for defense-in-depth).

findings.title: Permissionless order creation allows owner-attribution spoofing
findings.attack: mint_beacons_ok never checks the named owner signed, so an attacker mints a well-formed order attributed to an arbitrary victim's staking key (OwnerBeacon + My Orders), at the victim's personal order address.
findings.concrete_example: owner=VerificationKey(<victim stake key>), payment_address=<attacker>; order appears under victim's My Orders.
findings.impact: UI-level impersonation / My Orders pollution. Self-limiting: victim can cancel and keep attacker-funded offer+deposit. Not fund theft.
findings.recommended_fix: If attribution integrity matters, require list.has(self.extra_signatories, owner_key_hash) at mint (note: removes the permissionless-liquidity property; decide deliberately) or label externally-created orders in the UI.

findings.title: Route/arbitrage planners do not exclude the taker's own orders -> wash/self-fill
findings.attack: Neither planner filters candidates by owner; a user can be routed to take their own orders, producing wash volume and misleading average prices. On-chain valid, no fund risk.
findings.concrete_example: User with open sell orders runs Smart Fill on the same pair and is routed into their own liquidity.
findings.actual_result: Self-fill legs are planned and executable.
findings.impact: Wash trading, inflated volume metrics, misleading route economics. No theft.
findings.proof_of_concept: Code review: no ownerStakeCredential filter in candidate selection.
findings.regression_test: Planner test asserting own orders are excluded when caller owner is provided.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass the connected owner stake key into the planners; drop candidates whose ownerStakeCredential matches; warn on self-fill.

findings.title: Order discovery cost scales with self-fundable spam flood -> indexer/provider DoS
findings.attack: Discovery fetches all OrderBeacon holders then per-holder UTxOs; a griefer minting many orders across many personal addresses multiplies provider calls per sync.
findings.concrete_example: Thousands of cheap orders (F-02/F-03 make each distinct+cheap) inflate Blockfrost usage.
findings.actual_result: Higher provider load / staler book; deposit is the only limiter.
findings.impact: Provider quota exhaustion / slow book. Cache-only; builder re-validates on-chain. No fund risk.
findings.recommended_fix: Paginate/cap holders per sync, keep the confirmed-open short-circuit, rate-limit.

suspected.title: Partial fill can strand an ADA-offer continuation below ledger min-UTxO
suspected.note: Ledger-level rejection (liveness), not theft; add a builder guard rejecting partials that would underfund the continuation.

suspected.title: Reference-script UTxO trust
suspected.note: Wrong/malicious reference script is caught by the ledger (hash must match order address). Deployment-hygiene note only.

suspected.title: Indexer classifySpend does not sort beacon-bearing outputs before rank pairing
suspected.note: Relies on provider output ordering; backfillAncestry sorts, classifySpend does not. Cache-only; add a sort for parity.
